meta.source: Bendinelli (2013), undergraduate monograph, USP/ESALQ, section 4, following Brueckner and Van Dender (2008, Journal of Urban Economics 64, 288-295) and Brueckner (2002, American Economic Review 92, 1357-1375); figures after Cohen and Coughlin (2003) and Cohen, Coughlin and Ott (2009), redrawn
meta.equations: numbered as in the monograph, (1) to (12)

assumptions.statement: Demand is perfectly elastic at the total price p in equations (1)-(11); consumer surplus is zero and welfare is the airlines' joint profit.
Every seat is sold; s is exogenous and identical across the two airlines.
c' > 0 and c'' >= 0 (equation 5). Every bound on lambda is conditional on this.
Airline 1 leads and airline 2 follows by assumption; f1 > f2 is a consequence of who leads, not of size.
The tolls of (10)-(11) are per-flight constants evaluated at the efficient allocation; they are not assumed to alter the follower's reaction slope.
'Pressuposição 2' (the leader under inelastic demand sits between the two endpoint readings of (12)) needs -1 < df2/df1 <= -1/2, which holds iff c''/s >= s^2 d''.
assumptions.status: holds iff c''/s >= s^2 d''; verified symbolically for d'' = 0 and numerically for linear demand

assumptions.statement: 'Pressuposição 3' (entry of a low-cost carrier breaks the Stackelberg structure and the entrant has incentives to internalise its own congestion).
assumptions.status: verbal in the monograph; illustrated by this repository's Cournot extension

assumptions.statement: Existence and uniqueness of an interior equilibrium.
assumptions.status: verified numerically for the chosen parameters only

identities.statement: The efficient condition is p - tau - [F c'(F) + c(F)]/s = 0
The follower's condition is p - tau - [f2 c' + c]/s = 0
lambda = (1 + x)/(2 + x) with x = f2 c''/c'
lambda - 1/2 = x/(2(2 + x)) >= 0, so lambda >= 1/2
identities.method: symbolic: sign under the declared assumptions

identities.statement: 1 - lambda = 1/(2 + x) > 0, so lambda < 1
identities.method: symbolic: sign under the declared assumptions

identities.statement: lambda = 1/2 exactly when c'' = 0
The leader's condition is p - tau - (1/s)[f1 c'(1 + df2/df1) + c] = 0
At one point (7) and (9) give f1 = f2/(1 - lambda); with lambda = (1+x)/(2+x), f1 - 2 f2 = f2 x >= 0
F c' - f1 c'(1 - lambda) = (f2 + lambda f1) c'
(f2 - f1 df2/df1) c' = (f2 + lambda f1) MCD/(f1 + f2) when df2/df1 = -lambda
At f1 = f2 = f*: T1* = (1/2)(1 + lambda*) MCD*
With c'' = 0 (lambda* = 1/2) the leader's toll is 3/4 of MCD*, halfway between the Cournot toll (1/2) and the atomistic toll (1)
The follower's toll F c' - f2 c' = f1 c' is 1/2 MCD* at the symmetric optimum
A monopolist's condition coincides with the efficient one (full internalisation)
A Cournot duopolist's toll is the rival's flights times c', i.e. 1/2 MCD at symmetry
With p = d(sF): d + s f1 d'(1 + df2/df1) - tau - (1/s)[f1 c'(1 + df2/df1) + c] = 0
The efficient condition under inelastic demand is d - tau - [F c' + c]/s = 0
At df2/df1 = -1 the condition collapses to d - tau - c/s = 0
Under p = d(sF), df2/df1 = -A_/B_ with B_ = A_ + c'/s - s d'; and -df2/df1 - 1/2 = f2 (c''/s - s^2 d'')/(2 B_), so the bound <= -1/2 holds iff c''/s >= s^2 d''
With d'' = 0: df2/df1 = -(k + f2 c'')/(2k + f2 c''), k = c' - s^2 d' > 0, so the elastic-case bounds hold
c = a + bF: the efficient total is D/(2b)
c = a + bF: each Cournot duopolist flies D/(3b)
c = a + bF: the leader flies D/(2b) and the follower D/(4b)
c = a + bF: price-taking airlines fly D/b in total, twice the efficient total
c = a + bF: the welfare loss is 1/9 of W* under Cournot, 1/4 under Stackelberg and all of it under atomistic behaviour
c = a + bF, d = d0 - dd Q: f1 = Dp/(2m), f2 = Dp/(4m), F* = Dp/(s^2 dd + 2b)
At any Stackelberg equilibrium f2 = (1 - lambda) f1, so T1 = T2 = f1 c'

rows.theory_object: flight volumes in the congested (peak) period: f1 + f2 with c' > 0
rows.theory_object_pt: volumes de voo no pico: f1 + f2, com c' > 0
rows.rationale: more flights in congested hours raise c(F) and delays

rows.theory_object: flight volumes off peak: the period where the model puts no congestion
rows.theory_object_pt: volumes fora do pico: o período sem congestionamento no modelo
rows.rationale: the model predicts nothing here; the article finds the same positive sign as on peak

rows.theory_object: non-strategic delay: weather and airport restrictions
rows.theory_object_pt: atraso não estratégico: clima e restrições de aeroporto
atraso não estratégico: rotação de aeronave (código RA)

rows.theory_object: the airport's congestion state: delays of all carriers at the busier endpoint
rows.theory_object_pt: o estado de congestionamento do aeroporto: atrasos de todas as empresas na ponta mais movimentada
rows.rationale: c(F) is a function of everybody's traffic

rows.theory_object: market power on the route: d' < 0 in equation (12)
rows.theory_object_pt: poder de mercado na rota: d' < 0 na equação (12)
rows.rationale: ambiguous: the monograph's Table 1 expected '-, +'; the 2016 article reads it as the competition-quality channel

rows.theory_object: internalisation at the airport: the dominant carrier's own share of MCD, Proposition 1
rows.theory_object_pt: internalização no aeroporto: a parcela própria do dano marginal da dominante, Proposição 1
rows.rationale: a carrier that faces its own congestion restrains flights; the toll it needs is smaller

rows.theory_object: a low-cost carrier on the route: 'Pressuposição 3'
rows.rationale: the monograph's Table 1 expects both LCC dummies to reduce delays

rows.theory_object: a low-cost carrier at either endpoint city: the non-price spillover
rows.theory_object_pt: uma LCC em uma das cidades-extremo: o spillover não-preço
rows.rationale: same expectation, at the city rather than the route
